dataPoints._note: Ambiguous — floor 99 ≠ game 100. Sprint 27 concluded ceil. Explained: internal sum > displayed sum due to fractional stat accumulation from training.
Integer mean — floor and ceil agree. Not diagnostic.

Sprint 27 used displayed sum 2631. But Sprint 27 concluded ceil=176 ✓. HOWEVER: displayed sum was lower than internal sum — fractional training gains pushed internal sum high enough that floor(internal/15)=176 also. Not a clean test.
DECISIVE. Clean tier upgrade only — no training between snapshots. Integer stat changes. floor(2615/15)=floor(174.33)=174 ✓. ceil=175 ✗. Resolves ambiguity conclusively.

ovr_formula_verification.conclusion: Game uses Math.floor. Sprint 27's apparent ceil confirmation was an artefact: fractional stat accumulation from training inflated the internal sum above the displayed screenshot sum, making floor(internal) equal ceil(displayed) for those cases. The clean Grant T2→T3 tier upgrade (no training, integer-only stat changes) is the only unambiguous test. floor wins. Fixed in qualityPctToOvr() sprint 32.
ovr_formula_verification.macgregor_confirmation: MacGregor T2: displayed sum=2181, game OVR=145. floor(2181/15)=floor(145.4)=145 ✓. Consistent with floor formula.

bxps_recalibration.finding: bXPS=220 was calibrated against the stepped xpCostTable model in Sprint 24. Sprint 25 switched to exponential 2.94*exp(stat/55) without re-calibrating. The exponential model's compounding makes 60-stat-point gains significantly more expensive than the flat table entries, so bXPS needed to increase proportionally.

controlled_tests.note: Ratio 2.43 is sub-linear. Exponential cost model alone should give ~3.65 ratio for this stat range. Remaining 33% sub-linearity unexplained. Possible causes: (a) geometric session decay not yet applied in budget formula, (b) age-related reduction compounding with cost curve, (c) model K parameter off. Needs player age to resolve.
